Chapter 187: Recruiting People Also Requires Methods and Strategies

Li Ao's lecture at Peking University had limited student tickets.

There were too many students who wanted to attend, so it was impossible to distribute them. They could only be allocated to each class by proportion.

On average, each class only got two tickets.

When the spots were given to a class, the decision was basically made by drawing lots; otherwise, no matter how they were distributed, it would be unfair.

The Yuanpei Program was rather unlucky, with one hundred and forty or fifty people vying for those two tickets.

Chen Guiliang couldn't possibly take anyone's spot, so Director Zhu gave him a "hanging ticket," which meant he had to bring his own plastic stool and find a spot somewhere in an aisle.

In the morning, his dorm mates, Jiang Junlai, Tong Zhihong, and Li Heng, went to their classes in the academic building with resentful looks on their faces. None of them had managed to get a ticket.

Chen Guiliang timed his arrival at the auditorium in the administration building and found it was already packed with people.

Many students without tickets were holding various homemade banners, just like fans waiting for their idol. They planned to wait outside for the entire event. Especially outside the doors and windows, you could still hear what was being said inside.

One of the banners was particularly interesting: Brother Ao, welcome back!

The auditorium doors had already opened, and Chen Guiliang entered with his ticket and stool. He found a spot in the innermost aisle of the first row of the student section, trying his best not to disturb anyone.

After a few minutes of waiting, shouts came from outside, a scene truly reminiscent of fans chasing a star.

Accompanied by several university leaders, Li Ao had strolled over through the Peking University campus. Feeling the enthusiasm of the faculty and students, he said to the leader beside him, "I had originally prepared many sharp remarks, but this atmosphere makes me feel they aren't quite appropriate. Seeing everyone so enthusiastic, I've decided to speak more on milder topics."

Upon hearing this, the expressions of the several leaders visibly relaxed.

They chatted as they entered the auditorium and took their seats. Since it wasn't time yet, they sat there and continued their conversation.

"Bang, bang, bang, bang!"

The students outside couldn't wait any longer. They banged on the windowpanes and shouted, "Brother Ao, say a few words! Hurry and say something!"

A university leader chuckled, "It seems Professor Li is quite popular among the students."

Li Ao replied, "Wait until I'm done speaking. It won't be too late to praise me then."

The university leader didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

Soon, Li Ao walked onto the stage. "You can all finally see me. Directors, presidents, CEOs... all you kids... Am I nervous coming here to give a speech..."

"The night before last, I made up a story. A young lady from Beijing saw a man walking back and forth in a building, muttering to himself. The lady asked him, 'What are you doing?' He said, 'I'm going to give a speech at Peking University.' The lady asked, 'Are you nervous?' He said, 'I'm not nervous.' The lady said, 'If you're not nervous, why did you run into the women's restroom?'"

It was a very corny joke, but some people let out a chuckle.

Then, Li Ao added, "That man was Lien Chan!"

"Hahaha!"

The entire audience burst into laughter.

Because a few months ago, Lien Chan had also given a speech at Peking University.

Li Ao continued his tirade, "Lien Chan fooled you all... For those of you who think Lien Chan's speech was good, I must warn you, you might be very disappointed today..."

After a while, he took out the copy of Mao's Selected Works he carried with him and expounded on what true liberalism is.

The essence of true liberalism is, first, to look within oneself, and second, to seek recourse in the law.

To look within oneself means you must be self-critical and allow others to criticize you, instead of only freely criticizing others.

That is high-level liberalism.

The expressions of the several leaders, however, grew increasingly solemn, because some of Li Ao's words made them tense.

"...cannot be subdued by force, corrupted by wealth and honor, swayed by poverty and lowliness, or moved by fads. Thank you, everyone!"

He was finally done speaking. All the leaders breathed a collective sigh of relief.

Thunderous applause erupted both inside and outside the hall.

Chen Guiliang also clapped several times, especially during the part discussing liberalism. He thought it was brilliantly articulated.

The liberalism Li Ao believed in was a liberalism with limits, not the currently popular neoliberalism!

The leaders said a few more words, and then the student Q&A session began.

One student was very fierce, directly stating that a certain university leader was stifling academic freedom... That leader's expression turned very ugly.

Chen Guiliang raised his hand several times, and Li Ao finally said, "Give the microphone to the student in the aisle over there."

Many teachers and students had been focused on Li Ao, and only then did they notice Chen Guiliang hanging out there. A burst of laughter instantly erupted.

As a staff member passed the microphone over, Li Ao asked, "What are you all laughing at? Is this student very famous?"

Chen Guiliang took the microphone and stood up. "Today's speech was brilliant, and I generally agree with Mr. Li's views. However, I do have some objections, and I'm not sure if I can voice them."

Li Ao said, "As I just mentioned, liberalism requires allowing others to criticize oneself. If I said something wrong, feel free to speak up."

Chen Guiliang said, "Mr. Li told us not to curse the Beiyang warlords and to conduct a historical reflection. He even used the Beiyang warlords' invitation to Cai Yuanpei to be the president of Peking University as proof of their magnanimity. I believe this is highly inappropriate."

"How is it inappropriate?" Li Ao asked.

Chen Guiliang said:

"First, the Beiyang warlords had their good and bad points, and they were comprised of numerous factions, so they cannot be simply categorized. Even a single warlord could be both evil and benevolent. But overall, the Beiyang warlords are difficult to rehabilitate."

"Second, the person who invited Mr. Cai Yuanpei to be the president of Peking University was Fan Yuanlian. Mr. Fan was the first president of Beijing Normal University and one of the founders of Nankai University. He himself was anti-Beiyang. It was only because of the political struggle between the Presidential Palace and the State Council at the time that Duan Qirui, in order to win over more factions, invited Fan Yuanlian to be the Minister of Education."

"And when Mr. Cai was the Minister of Education in the south, he had invited Mr. Fan to be his Vice Minister of Education, responsible for taking over the educational resources left by the Qing dynasty. When Mr. Fan became the Minister of Education in the north, he would naturally invite Mr. Cai. If the Beiyang warlords truly had magnanimity, Mr. Cai would have been the Vice Minister of Education, not the president of Peking University."

"Mr. Fan and Duan Qirui were political allies. When Li Yuanhong drove Duan Qirui out, Mr. Fan couldn't keep his post, and Mr. Cai's position at Peking University also became difficult. At that time, Li Yuanhong was the nominal head of the Beiyang government. He did not tolerate Mr. Fan and Mr. Cai; on the contrary, he did everything he could to suppress them."

"Therefore, I believe Mr. Li's assertions about the Beiyang warlords are historically baseless and really cannot stand up to scrutiny. They are purely off-the-cuff remarks."

Li Ao adjusted his glasses, looking a little embarrassed, then smiled again. "This student has spoken very well, with reason and evidence. I humbly accept his criticism and retract my statements about the Beiyang warlords."

"Clap, clap, clap, clap!"

The teachers and students below the stage applauded enthusiastically.

After criticism naturally came praise.

Chen Guiliang continued, "Mr. Li's discourse on liberalism was brilliant. Certain people nowadays, and even some media outlets, only want freedom for themselves. They even go so far as to deprive others of their freedom for the sake of their own."

"Nothing in the world is absolute; everything is relative. I believe that for however much freedom a person enjoys, they should bear an equal amount of responsibility. Demanding freedom without bearing responsibility is pseudo-liberalism."

"To put it crudely, if you fart in a public place, you still have to bear the consequence of people giving you dirty looks. Speaking carries much more weight than farting. If a person's free speech causes severe consequences, I believe they must bear the corresponding responsibility."

"Of course, for some people and some media outlets today, what they say is worth even less than a fart!"

A wave of laughter and applause broke out from the audience.

Li Ao smiled, "That's not crude at all. Well said."

Chen Guiliang said, "I've said so much mainly just to get Mr. Li Ao's attention. I hope Mr. Li Ao can join Kaixin001, write some articles there, and discuss more topics with mainland netizens."

Li Ao was taken aback. "What kind of website is Kaixin001?"
